items.title: PM: Govt debt rises due to budget deficit, not new spending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied claims that the government is taking on new debt to finance its expenditure. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said government debt was cumulative, with each year's net borrowing adding to the outstanding debt from previous years. Anwar said annual new borrowing had declined from RM100 billion in 2022 to RM92.6 billion in 2023, RM76.8 billion in 2024 and RM75.6 billion in 2025.

items.title: Najib’s immediate family can stay with him during house arrest, Parliament told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Only immediate family members are permitted to reside in the same house as Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Razak under strict home detention conditions, which also prohibit the former prime minister from using personal mobile phones or appearing on social media, Parliament was told today. Speaking during Minister’s Question Time this morning, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail outlined the specific terms stipulated by the Pardons Board governing Najib’s residence, movement, and communications. Beyond that, prior written permission is required,” Saifuddin explained.

items.title: Saifuddin to propose declassifying Najib's pardon minutes at cabinet meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail will propose that the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting on Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon be declassified at tomorrow's cabinet meeting. He said the proposal by Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) was a good one, as it would allow the public to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the procedures surrounding the conditional pardon granted to the former prime minister. He was responding to Syed Saddiq's supplementary question on whether the government was prepared to declassify the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning Najib's conditional pardon.

items.title: Najib sought approval for second house under house arrest, says Saifuddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak had submitted a written request to be allowed to use a second residence while serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the request could not be accommodated yet as the Pardons Board had expressly designated No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, as Najib's residence under the conditional pardon order.

items.title: Nvidia shares plunge following reports CEO Huang could be ousted
items.summary: NEW YORK: Nvidia shares plunged on Wednesday following media reports that the US chipmaker's board was considering removing chief executive Jensen Huang, reported German news agency dpa. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources, reported that the Nvidia board could meet shortly to decide on Huang's future. According to the report, Huang and Nvidia initially declined to comment.

items.title: SP Setia earnings forecasts cut after results miss expectations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Research houses have cut their earnings forecasts for SP Setia Bhd after its third quarter (Q3) and nine-month results missed expectations. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) dropped its earnings forecast for the property developer by 13.9 per cent, 11.6 per cent and 10.2 per cent for financial year 2026 (FY26), FY27 and FY28, respectively, to factor in lower sales assumptions. The firm said SP Setia's core earnings for the cumulative nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2026, of RM75.9 million only accounted for 28.3 per cent of its full-year forecast and 21.7 per cent of consensus.

items.title: Japan's Mimura says markets shouldn't forget intervention risks as yen nears 160
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura on Thursday warned market participants that it's "too early to forget" this summer's intervention as the yen again edged towards the key 160-per-dollar level. "It's still too early to forget what happened this summer," he added, referring to Japan's yen-buying interventions in late July through early August, including one conducted jointly with the US. The dollar rose to 159.94 against the Japanese yen early Thursday morning, hitting its strongest in over two months, buoyed by growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates after hot US inflation data and hawkish remarks from policymakers.

items.title: Court allows 1MDB companies to use affidavit in bid to freeze Rosmah's assets
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today allowed an appeal by 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and 10 other companies to use an affidavit by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's former personal shopper in their bid to freeze her assets. A three-member bench led by Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab unanimously overturned a High Court decision barring the companies from relying on the affidavit affirmed by Singaporean Shabnam Naraindas Daswani. The appellate court ruled that the High Court judge had erred in dismissing the companies' application for leave to file the further affidavit.

items.title: Najib barred from media, political activities under house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak is prohibited from making media statements, appearing on social media platforms or participating in political activities while serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat that the conditions were among several restrictions imposed under the conditional pardon order issued by the Pardons Board. He said the conditions also included restrictions on movement, visitors and the use of telecommunications devices, as well as mandatory participation in rehabilitation and intervention programmes.

items.title: GST reintroduction not a political decision - Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's refusal to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) is driven by macroeconomic considerations rather than political reasons, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government remained concerned that reintroducing the broad-based consumption tax would place an additional burden on Malaysians whose incomes were still relatively low. He also questioned whether the government would consider incorporating GST features into a hybrid taxation system.

items.title: Najib allowed to live only with immediate family under house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak is only allowed to live with his immediate family members while serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the conditions stipulated by the Pardons Board allowed Najib to live with his wives, children, sons- and daughters-in-law, and grandchildren. Najib is also prohibited from receiving visitors without written permission.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM NOV 12, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Thursday as cautious investor sentiment persisted, despite overnight gains on Wall Street. The benchmark index opened 3.61 points lower at 1,591.58. Market sentiment remained subdued amid concerns over higher-than-expected October inflation data, which weighed on investor confidence.

items.title: Man arrested hours after stealing wallet from car in Cheras
items.summary: KAJANG: A man in his 20s was arrested after he was caught on closed-circuit television (CCTV) stealing a wallet from a car parked at a house in Taman Rakan, Cheras, yesterday. He said a review of CCTV footage showed an unidentified man entering the compound of the victim's house before taking the wallet, which contained his identity card, ATM card and debit card. Naazron said the victim lodged a police report at 10.15am yesterday.

items.title: Govt studies extending i-Sayang scheme to foreign wives
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government, through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), will continue to study a proposal to expand the scope and coverage of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives. The Finance Ministry (MOF) said the proposal would be studied carefully, taking into account the importance of protecting families' retirement savings and ensuring the programme's sustainability. "The government takes note of the proposal to expand the eligibility criteria for i-Sayang recipients to allow non-citizen wives to receive transferred contributions from their Malaysian citizen husbands.

items.title: Minimum wage hike should push businesses to improve productivity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's latest minimum wage increase is expected to benefit workers through better incomes, while encouraging businesses to step up efforts to improve productivity to ensure that higher wages can be sustained without putting further pressure on prices. CGS International Securities Malaysia chief economist Nazmi Idrus said wage growth had helped workers recover some of the purchasing power lost during the high-inflation period following the Covid-19 pandemic. According to Bank Negara Malaysia's Annual Report 2025, despite moderate inflation, many households continue to grapple with higher living costs amid slow wage growth.

items.title: MyNews targets 720 outlets by Q2 FY27
items.summary: As at end-October 2026, the convenience store operator had 712 outlets, as the company prioritised profitable store expansion following the closure of 69 underperforming outlets. "Mynews remains selective in choosing new store locations, prioritising productivity over network expansion, although it remains open to higher rental locations such as airports and shopping malls where sales potential is strong," CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said. However, the firm said rising rental, logistics and labour costs continue to weigh on Mynews' profitability despite improving sales momentum.

items.title: CelcomDigi steps up cyber and climate safeguards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd is strengthening its cybersecurity capabilities and climate resilience measures to mitigate growing digital threats and environmental risks as it seeks to safeguard its network operations and reputation, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The firm said the telecommunications company had stepped up customer protection efforts by flagging 260 million suspected scam calls and blocking 22 million SMS messages monthly amid rising digital scam threats. Analysts Choong Chen Foong and Kenny Lim said CelcomDigi's multi-layered cybersecurity strategy, which includes protection at both network and device levels, would help strengthen its ability to address emerging cyber threats.

items.title: General strike over housing brings out hundreds of thousands in Spain
items.summary: MADRID: Hundreds of thousands of protesters marched across Spain on Wednesday during a general strike over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election. Unions reported a significant response in some sectors in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, but business leaders played down the participation. Braving pouring rain, some 120,000 demonstrators marched through central Madrid carrying placards shaped like houses and chanting, "We have no home," as they called for more affordable housing, according to an estimate by the authorities.

items.title: UK house sales outlook is darkest since 2023
items.summary: LONDON: British property surveyors were the most downbeat about the short-term outlook for house sales in more than three years in October, as rising interest rates for mortgages compressed demand, a survey showed on Thursday. The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors said its outlook for house sales over the 12 months fell to -17 in October, with surveyors expecting the broadest drop in sales since July 2023. Its gauge of new buyer enquiries held at -24, while agreed sales fell to -24 from -18, the weakest in three months.

items.title: Beyond Buildings: BCB's vision for Malaysia's property landscape
items.summary: For BCB Bhd executive director Tan Lindy, the future of property development lies not just in delivering projects, but in creating communities that offer lasting value. At BCB, Tan is steering the group's property development direction while contributing to the wider real estate industry through her involvement in professional organisations. As executive director, Tan oversees BCB's property development projects and subsidiary companies, contributing to the group's business strategies and development initiatives.

items.title: Electricity bill protection expansion to cost RM248mil over 4 months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Expanding electricity bill protection to households consuming up to 800 kWh a month is expected to cost RM248 million over four months, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said. Fadillah, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation minister, said the measure would benefit about 90 per cent, or eight million, of domestic consumers in Peninsular Malaysia. He said the financial implications comprised three main components.

items.title: Govt spent RM70mil to host Bahrain F1 Grand Prix
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government spent RM70 million to host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) last month. Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the sum covered circuit maintenance and SIC's operating costs, while Bahrain bore the remaining expenses. He said hosting the race in Malaysia was estimated to cost RM350 million, including the rights fee and SIC's preparations.

items.title: Govt studies proposal to extend EPF i-Sayang scheme to non-citizen wives
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The government, through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), will continue to study a proposal to expand the scope and coverage of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives. “The government takes note of the proposal to expand the eligibility criteria for i-Sayang recipients to allow non-citizen wives to receive transferred contributions from their Malaysian citizen husbands. The MOF was responding to a question from Rodziah Ismail (PH-Ampang) on the strategies and implementation mechanisms for the proposed expansion of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives, given that non-citizen husbands are already allowed to do so for their Malaysian citizen wives.

items.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
items.summary: WASHINGTON: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage. With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year "lame duck" period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington. Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the US and Iran is unlikely.

items.title: Penang exco defends RM8.4b Perak water deal, says charge covers dedicated plant over 40 years
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — The Penang state government has defended the RM8.4 billion capacity charge under its conditional water supply agreement with Perak, saying the payment covers a treatment plant dedicated to the state and is spread over 40 years. State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the charge was a deferred payment for the construction and financing of the plant, which would be built solely to supply treated water to Penang. He said the conditional Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) between Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang Sdn Bhd (PBAPP) and Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd (PAIP) was a government-to-government agreement aimed at ensuring Penang's future water security.

items.title: Straight Path Convention returns for 13th edition with focus on influence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Straight Path Convention (TSP) returns for its 13th edition on Nov 14 and 15, focusing on how influence can strengthen Muslim identity and shape society. The annual English-language Islamic educational convention will be held at the Grand Banquet Hall, UTM Hotel & Residence, Kuala Lumpur, under the theme "INFLUENCE: Impact That Shapes Your Legacy". FIVE SPEAKERS FROM FIVE COUNTRIES This year's convention will feature five speakers from five countries: Dr Ali Albarghouthi (Canada), Dr Muhammad Salah (Egypt), Dr Abu Hafiz Salleh Hudin (Malaysia), Sheikh Hisham Abu Yusuf (United Kingdom) and Sheikh Wael Ibrahim (Australia).

items.title: Melaka polls: Lok puts community service at heart of Bandar Hilir campaign
items.summary: MELAKA: Unfazed by a three-cornered contest in an opposition stronghold, BN's Bandar Hilir candidate Jasmine Lok is banking on her years of grassroots service to win voters' support. The MCA candidate, who has served as a Melaka Historic City Council (MBMB) councillor since 2022, said her experience in community work had given her the confidence to serve the constituency. My confidence comes from working on the ground since 2011," said Lok.

items.title: Record crowd greets Pope Leo as he calls Peru his homeland in emotional visit
items.summary: LIMA: Pope Leo was greeted by the largest crowd of his papacy in an emotional return to Peru on Wednesday, declaring the South American country where he served as a missionary for two decades his homeland. The huge crowds, estimated at 3 million by local officials, pressed against police and security barriers, waving balloons and flags and chanting "Leo, Leo, Leo". In a closely watched speech to President Keiko Fujimori shortly after being greeted in Lima, the first Peruvian citizen to lead the Catholic Church urged the president to build confidence among her people after her narrow election victory earlier this year, and alluded to the contested legacy of her father, the late former president Alberto Fujimori.

items.title: 211 companies deactivated from eCOSS for non-compliance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 211 companies had their access to the Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme System (eCOSS) deactivated as of Oct 30 for failing to comply with the terms and conditions governing the distribution and sale of subsidised packet cooking oil. The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry also recorded eight cases of violations involving the sale and purchase of subsidised packet cooking oil by foreigners following the introduction of the Mobile eCOSS system and the enforcement of related regulations on March 1. Of the total, 2,763 cases involved diesel, with seizures valued at RM59.67 million, followed by 1,722 petrol-related cases (RM5.43 million) and 1,408 cases involving packet cooking oil (RM17.74 million).

items.title: Four suspects rob man of RM10,000 after approaching him for donations at Permatang Pauh petrol station
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 12 — A 43-year-old man was injured after being robbed by four individuals believed to be foreigners using sharp metal objects at the entrance to a petrol station along Jalan Samagagah, Permatang Pauh, here yesterday. Seberang Perai Tengah district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the incident, which occurred at about 11.30am, was believed to have involved two men and two women suspected to be foreigners from Central Asian countries. “In the incident, the suspects are believed to have acted aggressively and used sharp metal objects, causing injuries to the victim before fleeing with his personal belongings, with total losses estimated at RM10,000.

items.title: ‘When in doubt, shoot’: KL police chief orders men not to hesitate following machete attack on constable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus has directed officers never to hesitate in drawing and discharging their service firearms against violent resistance, following a vicious machete attack on Wednesday that severed a policeman's hand. Fadil stressed that frontline personnel must take immediate defensive action to protect their lives rather than risk suffering the same catastrophic harm. You must know how to draw your weapons: Ready, draw, fire.

items.title: Malaysian Bar mounts fresh challenge against Najib’s house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has filed a fresh legal action challenging the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest. The Bar filed the application for leave of judicial review on November 10 at the High Court here, naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents. In the application, the Bar seeks a declaration that any proceedings or decision purportedly made under Articles 40 and 42 of the Federal Constitution is invalid in law and contradicts the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Court of Appeal clears Felda Palm Industries of effluent discharge offence, orders RM18,000 refund
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 12 — The Court of Appeal yesterday set aside Felda Palm Industries Sdn Bhd's conviction and RM18,000 fine for discharging effluent with content exceeding the prescribed limits. A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Noorin Badaruddin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid allowed the company’s appeal to set aside the Sessions Court decision that convicted it of the offence and imposed the fine. On August 8, 2023, the Sessions Court convicted Felda Palm Industries and imposed an RM18,000 fine, with 30 days' imprisonment in default of payment, while the High Court dismissed the company's appeal and upheld the Sessions Court's decision on January 16 this year.

items.title: AI is increasing the speed of cyberattacks, insurance panel says
items.summary: Initial demands have reached as high as US$500 million, with confirmed payments as high as US$90 million. New threats, including social engineering fraud, have emerged in recent years, forcing cyber insurers to adapt. Humans are often the way in for threat actors, Kulikowski said.

items.title: ‘A man of principle’: Ramanan says Anthony Loke’s resignation a major loss for govt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has described Anthony Loke Siew Fook’s decision to resign as Transport Minister as a major loss to the government. This is a major loss,” he said here yesterday. Yesterday, Loke announced his immediate resignation as Transport Minister following the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.

items.title: Penang approves emergency slope works at Paya Terubong landslide site
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Emergency slope stabilisation works have been approved at the Taman Seri Rambai landslide site in Paya Terubong following the submission of a complete engineering proposal. State Local Government, Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) received the complete documentation and formal application from Aptitude Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd yesterday. "Following the submission, DOSH has granted permission for the developer's civil engineer to carry out the mitigation works, subject to approvals and clearances from other relevant agencies," he said today.

items.title: Pan Borneo Highway delays not always contractors’ fault, says Nanta
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Contracts of companies involved in the construction of the Pan Borneo Highway cannot be terminated arbitrarily, as delays in individual work packages are not necessarily caused solely by the contractors’ shortcomings. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said that when contractors applied for an extension of time (EOT), the Works Ministry (KKR) had to assess whether the delays were caused by constraints on the part of government agencies or other factors. He said only one contractor had so far had its contract terminated over delays in the project, following a comprehensive assessment.

items.title: Paya Terubong landslide: Four evacuated homes to remain off-limits for up to five months
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — Residents of four evacuated houses in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, will not be allowed to return home until mitigation works at the landslide site are completed, state executive councillor H’ng Mooi Lye said today. The local government and town and country planning committee chairman said the works were expected to take four to five months. "The mitigation works permitted by DOSH include emergency surface drainage mitigation works (ESCP) and slope stabilisation in the landslide area (Zone 1), as well as preventive stabilisation works on the exposed cut slopes at the construction site," he said.

items.title: Najib's conditional pardon: Johor MB tells DAP, Amanah to seek Anwar's explanation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said DAP and Amanah leaders, as well as the Bar Council, should seek clarification from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon and house arrest , instead of involving the palace. Onn Hafiz said Anwar had brought forward and included the pardon application for Najib in the agenda of the Pardons Board meeting during a Dewan Rakyat sitting on Dec 10, 2024. Earlier, media reports said Tony Pua had allegedly mocked the King over the conditional pardon granted to Najib.

items.title: Ramanan: HR Ministry to table new commuter protection, post-maternity allowance in December
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Amendments to the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017 (Act 789) and the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800) will be tabled in Parliament in December. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the proposed amendments to Act 789 would involve the Commuter Scheme, while those to Act 800 would cover the Post-Maternity Leave Allowance (EPCB). He said the amendments to Act 789 were aimed at strengthening social protection for Malaysians who commute across borders for work, particularly the more than 400,000 Malaysians who travel to Singapore daily.

items.title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak rise to 1,444
items.summary: According to the Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal, Selangor recorded the highest number, with 1,138 evacuees from 315 families housed at seven relief centres in Kuala Selangor. Perak recorded 302 evacuees from 91 families at two relief centres in Hilir Perak. Of the total evacuees, 466 were adult women, 437 adult men, 219 girls, 283 boys, 27 baby boys and 12 baby girls.

items.title: Anwar says RM7.5b Budget allocation will help Bumiputera contractors expand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The increase in Budget 2027 funding for Bumiputera G1 to G4 contractors to RM7.5 billion aims to help small contractors build their capabilities, expand their businesses and undertake projects needed by the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said in a Facebook post yesterday that the allocation had been discussed during an engagement session with representatives of Bumiputera contractors’ associations, which focused on ensuring the budget initiatives benefited small contractors. “I want these opportunities to help produce more competitive and ethical Bumiputera contractors.

items.title: Zahid says Negeri Sembilan political crisis in final stage, solution expected soon
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 12 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi is confident that the political crisis in Negeri Sembilan will be resolved soon. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, was speaking at the Perikatan Nasional (PN)-BN Grand Finale Ceramah programme here last night. Also present were PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man and Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.

items.title: Cabinet reshuffle no reason to dissolve Parliament, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The dissolution of Parliament should not be proposed simply because of questions surrounding a Cabinet reshuffle when the government remains functional and commands majority support, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh. She said that after nearly four years of the Unity Government, the country should be able to focus on more pressing priorities, including investment, job opportunities, the cost of living and the long-standing institutional reform agenda. “A Cabinet reshuffle is part of the process of strengthening the administration.

items.title: Guan Eng says two-year push for non-Bumi funding has failed to sway Anwar, but will keep pressing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today said his repeated appeals to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the past two years for additional government allocations for non-Bumiputera communities have been unsuccessful. The Bagan MP said he had personally raised the proposal with Anwar during meetings and in Parliament, amid criticism from political activists over his failure to secure the allocations. Despite the setback, Lim said Anwar had adopted ten other economic proposals following repeated appeals from him and senior DAP leaders.

items.title: Anwar calls for firm action after policeman’s wrist severed in Kepong attack
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned the attack on a policeman whose right wrist was severed by a foreign national in Kepong yesterday afternoon. Anwar said all forms of crime and violence, particularly against enforcement personnel tasked with protecting public safety, were entirely unacceptable. Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said yesterday that the police personnel was being treated at Kuala Lumpur Hospital and was in stable condition.

items.title: Suspect shot dead after severing policeman’s wrist with machete in Kepong (VIDEO)
items.summary: Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said police received a report from a member of the public at 4pm about a man who was reportedly in an unstable condition and behaving aggressively. “Several firefighters and MOH personnel also sustained minor injuries. Shazeli said the suspect attacked police with a machete when officers tried to arrest him, prompting them to fire several shots.

items.title: Still paying for an unfinished home in Malaysia? Here’s what Budget 2027 offers affected buyers
items.summary: Budget 2027 proposes measures to ease some of these costs and encourage developers to revive abandoned housing projects. What qualifies as an abandoned housing project? As of August 31, 2026, the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) had identified 262 abandoned private housing projects in Peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: Flood season brings lucrative catfish haul for Kinta river fishermen in Perak
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, Nov 12 — Whenever the water level of the Kinta River rises during the rainy season, Anuar Osman knows it is time to head to the river and set up belat (traditional fish traps) in anticipation of the arrival of ikan lundu (a type of catfish), which provides him with a supplementary source of income. For the 49-year-old inland fisherman, catching ikan lundu is not his main occupation but rather a seasonal opportunity that he seizes whenever the fish migrate in schools through the river. Anuar, who also manages an oil palm smallholding, said the large-scale appearance of ikan lundu typically lasts for about a week, depending on the river’s water level.

items.title: Cabinet to be briefed on latest constitutional amendments separating AG, Public Prosecutor roles
items.summary: The meeting was chaired by Pengerang Member of Parliament, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. Also present were Parit Sulong MP and Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, William Leong Jee Keen (Selayang), Syahredzan Johan (Bangi), Ramkarpal Singh (Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (Beluran), Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (Kota Bharu) and Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muar). Larut MP and Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin, Alor Gajah MP and Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Datuk Lo Su Fui (Tawau) and Roy Angau Gingkoi (Lubok Antu) were unable to attend the meeting due to unavoidable circumstances.

items.title: Anwar, Wan Azizah convey condolences over Melaka PKR leader J. Samivel’s passing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail have extended their condolences to the family of Alor Gajah PKR branch vice-chief J. Samivel, who died in a road accident in Jasin earlier today. Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, said in a Facebook post today that Samivel, 62, was also the representative for P. Denesh, the PH candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka state election. Jasin police chief Supt Lee Robert said police received a report about the accident involving the car Samivel was travelling in at Jalan Pondok Batang, Jasin, at about 12.45 pm today.

items.title: Nine-year-old boy killed in suspected crocodile attack in Kudat
items.summary: KUDAT, Nov 11 — A nine-year-old boy was killed in a suspected crocodile attack while trying to retrieve a fishing hook caught in Sungai Semayan, Kampung Semayan, Pulau Banggi, today. The victim, identified as Mohamad Hilmi Nurjahid, was a Year Three pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan Semayan. Kudat District Police Chief Supt Mohd Haris Ibrahim said the incident occurred at about 3.30pm while the boy was fishing with his elder brother.

items.title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s leap to 27th globally in digital, AI competitiveness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Malaysia has climbed seven rungs to 27th place out of 70 economies in the IMD World Digital and AI Ranking (WDAIR) 2026 from 34th place last year, becoming the second-highest-ranked country in ASEAN after Singapore. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was driven particularly by a 21-place improvement in artificial intelligence (AI) adoption to 14th place globally, a 10-place improvement in efficiency to 28th place, and Malaysia’s implementation of the national AI strategy, which ranked 12th. “Malaysia also ranks 18th in workforce development, second globally in graduates in sciences, fifth in venture capital, sixth in high-tech exports and eighth in investment incentives for AI.

items.title: Stay away from 14 Hulu Selangor rivers, waterfalls amid water surge danger, Fire Dept warns; Pertak, Siling, Batang Kali top hotspots
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR, Nov 11 — Fourteen recreational areas in Hulu Selangor have been identified as high-risk locations for water surges, with Sungai Pertak, Sungai Siling and Sungai Batang Kali emerging as the three main hotspots. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said Sungai Batang Kali recorded four water surge incidents this year, followed by Sungai Siling with three and Sungai Pertak with two. He said the other 11 high-risk locations were Lata Medang in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Inki in Kalumpang, River View Sungai Bernam in Hulu Selangor, Sungai Sendat and Sungai Tua in Ulu Yam, Sungai Kedondong in Batang Kali, Sungai Cilin in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Pinang in Batang Kali, Air Terjun Serendah in Serendah, Air Terjun Semangkuk and Sungai Liam in Hulu Selangor.

items.title: IGP says Prisons Dept responsible for Najib’s home security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Prisons Department is fully responsible for the security arrangements for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, who has been serving the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here since yesterday. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as a law enforcement agency, maintained close cooperation with the Prisons Department to ensure compliance with the security requirements. Mohd Khalid said PDRM had assigned several officers to assist the Prisons Department throughout the former prime minister’s period of serving the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: Government steps in with RM15m monthly subsidy as palm oil costs rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government has approved a special incentive of about RM15 million a month under the Cooking Oil Price Control Mechanism (MKHMM) to maintain ceiling prices and ensure a stable supply of bottled pure palm cooking oil. Armizan said the sustained increase in global CPO prices since June 2025 had placed mounting cost pressures on manufacturers, prompting some companies to halt production of bottled cooking oil. Meanwhile, PRESMA president Datuk Mohammed Mosin Abdul Razak said stable cooking oil prices would help restaurant operators better manage their business costs.

items.title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal Jalan Kuching crash that killed lorry driver
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A car washer was brought before the Magistrate’s Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month. He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44am on November 4. Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.

items.title: Azalina: Land acquisition must uphold rule of law, respect constitutional safeguards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Challenging decisions involving compulsory land acquisition is not an act of disloyalty but an essential part of upholding the rule of law, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said that as Malaysia continued to pursue economic growth and modernise its infrastructure, compulsory land acquisition remained a necessary but sensitive public duty requiring transparency, procedural fairness and adequate compensation. “From the perspective of democracy, challenging the exercise of power is not an act of disloyalty, rather it’s an essential part of the rule of law,” she said at the “Challenging Land Acquisition in Malaysia” book launch here today.

items.title: Nadma deploys 102,000 personnel ahead of 2026/2027 northeast monsoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has mobilised nearly 102,000 personnel from various departments and agencies, along with 40,000 operational assets, in preparation for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL). Nadma Deputy Director of Operations Datuk Dr Abdul Gapar Abu Bakar said the preparations also included 8,321 temporary relief centres nationwide, with a combined capacity of up to 1.9 million flood victims. Commenting on ground-level operational coordination, Abdul Gapar said district officers are responsible for mobilising initial flood response by activating the District Disaster Operations Control Centre.

items.title: Tragedy on the Melaka campaign trail: Car hits lorry, Alor Gajah PKR deputy chief dies in crash outside campaign operations room
items.summary: JASIN, Nov 11 — An aide of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka election was killed today when the car he was driving collided with a lorry, three days to voting day. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, paid tribute to J. Samivel, 62, in a Facebook post today, noting that the deceased was also Alor Gajah PKR deputy division chief. Brother Samivel, the representative of the Harapan candidate for the Asahan state seat, was killed in a road accident this afternoon.
